titulo: The imperative: asking, telling and instructing: The formal imperative: Sie

aula.titulo: The imperative: asking, telling and instructing
aula.objetivo: Form the imperative with «Sie», «wir», «du» and «ihr», including separable and irregular verbs, and understand the instructions in classes, textbooks and exams.

blocos.texto: Lesson goal. By the end of the four sessions, you conjugate sprechen, essen, geben, nehmen, lesen, sehen, helfen, fahren and schlafen without falling into the du/er trap, and you give orders, advice and requests with the imperative for du, ihr and Sie.

blocos.contexto: Camila and Jonas are making pasta. Lena arrives. Then the neighbor knocks on the door.

linhas.ru: — Camila, ich lese die Anleitung. Du nimmst die Tomaten.
linhas.pt: — Camila, I'll read the recipe. You get the tomatoes.
linhas.audio: Camila, ich lese die Anleitung. Du nimmst die Tomaten.

linhas.ru: — Gut. Und ich möchte ein Messer.
linhas.pt: — OK. And I want a knife.
linhas.audio: Gut. Und ich möchte ein Messer.

linhas.ru: — Hier, nimm das Messer! Und schneide die Zwiebel, bitte.
linhas.pt: — Here, take the knife! And chop the onion, please.
linhas.audio: Hier, nimm das Messer! Und schneide die Zwiebel, bitte.

linhas.pt: — Hi! What are you two doing?

linhas.ru: — Wir kochen. Lena, hilf mir bitte! Gib mir das Salz.
linhas.pt: — We're cooking. Lena, help me, please! Pass me the salt.
linhas.audio: Wir kochen. Lena, hilf mir bitte! Gib mir das Salz.

linhas.pt: — Do you eat pasta too, Lena?

linhas.ru: — Ja, gern. Ich esse viel, aber danach schlafe ich auf dem Sofa!
linhas.pt: — Yes, gladly. I eat a lot, but then I fall asleep on the sofa!
linhas.audio: Ja, gern. Ich esse viel, aber danach schlafe ich auf dem Sofa!

linhas.ru: — Das stimmt. Du schläfst immer sofort.
linhas.pt: — True. You always fall asleep right away.
linhas.audio: Das stimmt. Du schläfst immer sofort.

linhas.ru: — Entschuldigung! Seid bitte leise. Es ist schon spät.
linhas.pt: — Excuse me! Please be quiet. It's already late.
linhas.audio: Entschuldigung! Seid bitte leise. Es ist schon spät.

linhas.ru: — Oh, Entschuldigung, Herr Weber! Möchten Sie Pasta? Nehmen Sie einen Teller!
linhas.pt: — Oh, sorry, Mr. Weber! Would you like some pasta? Take a plate!
linhas.audio: Oh, Entschuldigung, Herr Weber! Möchten Sie Pasta? Nehmen Sie einen Teller!

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the vowel changes only with du and er/sie/es. With ich, wir, ihr and sie, the verb stays as in the infinitive.
blocos.comparacao: Three traps. English has one command form for everyone ("Speak slowly!"); German has three, depending on who you're talking to — and the du form keeps the vowel change.

tabela.ingles: Speak slowly! (to a group of friends)

itens.pt: to sit down, take a seat

blocos.titulo: The imperative with «Sie» and «wir», step by step
blocos.explicacao: The imperative is for asking, giving instructions, inviting and telling people what to do. We start with the POLITE form, which you hear in shops, schools and exams. STEP 1: take the infinitive («öffnen») and put «Sie» after it: «Öffnen Sie das Buch.» So the verb comes FIRST and «Sie» right behind it. English drops the "you" in commands; German formal commands keep it. STEP 2: separable verbs: the prefix goes to the END: «Hören Sie zu.», «Stehen Sie auf.» STEP 3: «bitte» makes the request polite and can go in several places: «Öffnen Sie bitte das Buch.» STEP 4: the «wir» form invites people to do something together — the German "let's": «Gehen wir!» (Let's go!), «Fangen wir an!» (Let's begin!). STEP 5: to negate, put «nicht» at the end: «Rauchen Sie nicht!»
blocos.comparacao: English commands drop the subject: "Open the book." The German formal imperative keeps it, right after the verb: «Öffnen Sie das Buch» — almost a question without the question mark. And "let's…" is simply the wir form with the verb first: «Gehen wir!»

erros.motivo: In the imperative, the verb comes BEFORE «Sie».
The separable prefix goes to the end.

blocos.enunciado: Give 5 instructions out loud as if you were a teacher: «Öffnen Sie …, Lesen Sie …, Schreiben Sie …»
Write the «ich» and «du» forms of «müssen», «wollen» and «dürfen».
